outcome: stage II or greater prolapse based on POP-Q
cohort: The study included 159 parous Ugandan women with a median age of 35 years and a median parity of 4.
finding: Pelvic floor disorders are prevalent among parous Ugandan women, with cesarean section appearing to be a protective factor.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was found to have a protective effect for the development of pelvic floor disorders.
